notes:
One character, one voice.

Casting was splitting a single person's speech across two voices — three bubbles of one sentence read by two different narrators. It now only tells speakers apart when a panel really holds two bubbles side by side, which is two people facing each other. A page without one is read in a single voice.

Still a best guess: it can be wrong when one character's bubbles wander across a page. Properly telling speakers apart means reading each bubble's tail, which is coming.
